doc.title: Ray Ricker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 27, 2022

title: How he approaches arranging and capturing ideas
summary: Ricker hums ideas first, needs a reason to arrange a tune, and keeps an Ideas notebook.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you about some of the other Legos that you’ve been able to construct and — arranging and composing — can you tell me where, first of all let’s talk about arranging. If you got a commission or you heard a tune that you wanted to arrange, let’s say for jazz ensemble, how do you go about thinking of a different way to set it so that you’re not just producing the original recording? Where do those thoughts come from?

Well I don’t know. I just start humming stuff, to tell you the truth. You know? What could it be? I can’t think of an example off the top of my head right now, but you have to — there’s got to be a reason that you do an arrangement. Let’s say I get to choose the tune that I want to do. There’s got to be a reason that I choose that tune. What am I going to bring to that tune that hasn’t been done umpteen million times before? What can I do? So I think about it that way. Usually I’m thinking, I’m humming those type of things in my head before I get to — hey I think maybe I’ll do an arrangement of that you know. I don’t think first and find a title in something, although sometimes it happens. They say do an arrangement on so-and-so you know, and you’ve got to make it fit them, you know
fit the person who is asking for it. That’s a difficult question. I don’t know exactly how that goes.

That’s okay because I think that’s sort of the magic of what makes people successful is they come up with things and they can’t explain why but that’s what makes them unique. Do you ever get ideas away from a piano or away from, okay I’m doing music now, but sometimes ideas may come at other times.

Oh yeah. Oh yeah, just riding in the car or something you know, thinking of a bass line or something like that. I know people that try to write them down as soon as they can, they just have a little notebook of — in fact I kept a notebook for a long time just called “Ideas” and I’d just write stuff down where you know it could be a big band chart on so- and-so and stuff like that. And then I’d come back to that and look at it say oh yeah that could work and then I’d go ahead and sketch it out and go from there.
